Your furnace has been sitting idle since spring. The first cold night is a bad time to find out it won't start.

Here's a short fall homeowner checklist worth doing this month 🍂

1. Book HVAC maintenance for your furnace or heat pump before the busy season.
2. Swap the HVAC filter. Many need changing every 1 to 3 months, so check the label on yours.
3. Clear the gutters once most of the leaves are down.
4. Disconnect garden hoses and shut off outdoor faucets before the first freeze.
5. Test your smoke and CO detectors.
6. Run the generator for a few minutes so it's ready for winter outages.

None of these jobs is hard. The hard part is remembering all of them, every year.

That's what I'm building Homvi for. It's a home maintenance app where every asset gets its own service schedule and a reminder before it's due.

It's the first chilly morning. You turn on the heat, and the house smells like something is burning.

Do you call someone, or wait it out?

That's exactly the kind of moment Homvi's AI assistant is for. Ask in plain words, the way you'd text a friend who knows houses, and get a clear answer: a dusty smell the first time the heat runs after months off is common and usually fades. If it lingers or smells electrical, switch the system off and get it checked.

It handles the everyday home maintenance questions we all end up searching for, from when to service the AC to what's worth doing before winter. It can also give you a budget estimate for the maintenance coming up each quarter, so costs don't land as a surprise.

Your AC wants attention every season. Your water purifier filter, every few months. Your car, by the mile. Your solar panels and generator, on clocks of their own.

Nobody can hold all of that in their head.

So most of us don't. We wait for a warning light, a strange noise, or water that suddenly tastes off. That's when maintenance quietly turns into repair.

Homvi gives every asset in your home its own service schedule. Add your AC or HVAC, RO purifier, car or EV, solar panels and generator, and each one gets its own reminders. The dashboard shows what's overdue, what's due soon and what's healthy, so you always know what to do next.

One home maintenance app instead of a dozen mental notes.

The easiest home screen to build for Homvi would have been a list of every task for every appliance in your house.

Accurate. And completely overwhelming.

Nobody wants to open an app to a wall of chores. So I made a design decision: lead with one number. The Home Health Score sums up how your home is doing. Right under it sit three counts, overdue, due soon and healthy. Only after that comes the task list.

The test I keep coming back to: you should know in two seconds whether your home needs you today. If everything is green, close the app and enjoy your weekend.

Building in public means sharing calls like this before launch, while they can still change. Homvi is coming soon to Google Play.
